summary: Hospitality operations: guest requests routed to housekeeping, maintenance, kitchen and front desk, with rooms, staff on duty and who is handling what.

actions.name: list_requests
actions.title: List guest requests
actions.description: Lists guest requests, newest first: request, room, department, priority, status (new, assigned, in_progress, done, cancelled; empty means new), assignee, guest and note. Filter by status, department or room. An empty result does not mean there are none: say the list is unavailable and ask for the request ID or name, or check the Board.

actions.name: get_request
actions.title: Read a guest request
actions.description: Reads one guest request by its row id: request, room, department, priority, status, assignee, guest and note.

actions.name: create_request
actions.title: Log a guest request
actions.description: Logs a new guest request for a room, e.g. room 204: two extra towels. department is housekeeping, maintenance, food or front_desk; priority is low, normal, high or urgent (urgent only for safety or a room the guest cannot use). source is desk, guest_form or workpeg_ai. Leave status empty: a new request is new.

actions.name: update_request
actions.title: Update a guest request
actions.description: Changes a guest request by row id. To assign: status assigned, assignee a name exactly as list_staff gives it, and assignee_email that person's email. Other statuses: in_progress, done, cancelled. Can also change priority or add a note. After an assignment, the assignee is told by email with peg_emails.send_email.

actions.name: list_rooms
actions.title: List rooms
actions.description: Lists rooms with floor, status (available, occupied, cleaning, maintenance) and guest. Filter by status, e.g. cleaning for rooms not ready yet. An empty result does not mean there are none: say the list is unavailable and ask for the room name, or check the Board.

actions.name: update_room
actions.title: Change a room
actions.description: Changes a room by its number or row id: status (available, occupied, cleaning, maintenance) or guest. maintenance takes it out of service.

actions.name: list_staff
actions.title: List staff
actions.description: Lists staff with email, department (housekeeping, maintenance, food, front_desk) and whether they are on duty. Filter by department or on_duty. An empty result does not mean there are none: say the list is unavailable and ask for the person's name and email, or check the Staff page.

skills.name: shift-handover
skills.title: Shift handover
skills.instructions:
Shift handover for NEXORA.

Use this at shift change or when someone asks for a handover, a shift report or what is still open.

1. Gather facts with the read tools only: list_requests (status new, then assigned, then in_progress), list_staff with on_duty true, and list_rooms with status cleaning and then maintenance. Use only what they return; never invent requests, rooms or names. If they return nothing, do not report that NEXORA is empty: say the lists are unavailable right now, ask for the request IDs to cover, and read each with get_request. Name a request by room and request, e.g. Room 311 - AC not cooling.

2. Write the handover, short and scannable:
- Headline: totals of new, assigned and in progress.
- Unassigned (status new or empty): room, request, department, priority. Urgent and high first.
- In hand: room, request, who has it.
- Rooms not ready: cleaning or out of service.
Leave out empty sections.

3. Propose an owner for each unassigned request: someone on duty in the matching department, preferring whoever has the fewest requests already. If nobody suitable is on duty, say so and suggest the duty manager. Show proposals as a numbered list.

4. Act only after the person confirms which to apply. For each, call update_request with status assigned, assignee the name exactly as list_staff gave it, and assignee_email that person's email. Report each result; one failure does not stop the rest. Then email each person you assigned, with peg_emails.send_email: to their email from list_staff (or the email the person gave you), subject "New task: <room> - <request>", and a short body naming the room, the request, the team and the priority, ending "Open My tasks in NEXORA to start it." Skip anyone without an email and say so. Report which emails were sent.

Be brief and factual: tired staff read this at shift change.

skills.name: guest-requests
skills.title: Guest requests from the guest form
skills.instructions:
Guest requests from the guest form, for NEXORA.

Guests have no Workpeg account. They send requests through a public form made with the Forms peg (formnow.now), usually opened from a QR code in the room. Use this skill to set that form up, to bring new answers into NEXORA, and to tell guests when their request is done.

A. Set up the guest form (only when asked, and only once)
1. Call peg_forms.list_forms. If a form titled "Guest requests" exists, use it and say so; do not make another.
2. Call list_rooms to get the room and space names exactly as NEXORA has them.
3. Call peg_forms.create_form with title "Guest requests", description "Tell us what you need and the team will take care of it.", confirmation "Thank you! The team has your request.", and questions as a JSON list:
   q1 "Your room or space", kind dropdown, required, options: every room name from list_rooms, one per line.
   q2 "What do you need?", kind paragraph, required, help "For example: two extra towels, or the AC is not cooling."
   q3 "Your name", kind short, not required.
   q4 "Email for updates (optional)", kind email, not required.
   Never ask for a password, code, card number or ID number.
4. A new form is a Draft. Ask the person before publishing. When they agree, call peg_forms.update_form with status Published, and explain that it goes live on formnow.now the next time someone opens the Forms peg, and that the link appears in peg_forms.list_forms then. Never make a link up.

B. Bring new guest answers into NEXORA
1. Call peg_forms.list_responses filtered by form_title "Guest requests".
2. Call list_requests and read each request's note. A response is already imported when a request's note contains "Guest form, submitted <its submitted_at>". Skip those, so nothing is logged twice.
3. For each new response, read the room, the request, the name and the email from its summary. Choose the department: housekeeping for towels, cleaning, linen and amenities; maintenance for anything broken, leaking, AC, power, door locks or keys; food for food and drink; front_desk for transport, checkout, bookings, spa, wake-up calls and anything else. Choose priority: urgent only for safety or a room the guest cannot use (for example locked out); high for a broken AC, no water or a door that will not open; otherwise normal.
4. Show the person the list you are about to log (room, request, team, priority) and ask before writing.
5. Then call create_request for each one: room exactly as the guest chose it, title a short clean version of what they asked, department, priority, guest their name if given, source guest_form, and note "Guest form, submitted <submitted_at>" followed by "Email: <email>" when they gave one.
6. Report what was logged, and suggest who to assign using list_staff (on duty, matching department, fewest open requests). When the person agrees, call update_request with status assigned, assignee and assignee_email. Then email each person you assigned, with peg_emails.send_email: to their email from list_staff (or the email the person gave you), subject "New task: <room> - <request>", and a short body naming the room, the request, the team and the priority, ending "Open My tasks in NEXORA to start it." Skip anyone without an email and say so. Report which emails were sent.

C. Tell the guest it is done
1. Only when the person asks, or confirms when you offer: for a request whose status is done and whose note has "Email: <address>", draft a short, friendly email and show it before sending.
2. Send it with peg_emails.send_email: to that address, subject "Your request is done", body naming the room and the request, thanking them, and signed with the business name. Never email anyone who did not give their address on the form.

Be brief and factual. Never invent responses, rooms, names or emails.
